b.x: If the middle ring weighs like a move, you do not leave. If the inner one looks like an arsenal, you are a stage on the street. No molle, no patch, no shop-window knife. A tool only if it is legal. The list to tick, ring by ring, is in Kits. The first-aid kit is another box, already written.

What leaves every morning and fits a pocket or an ordinary bag. Photo ID. Small cash, not a wad. One card. A charged phone. A small light that is not the phone’s torch. The next 24 hours of medicine. Keys. One bandage and a tissue. If it does not fit, it is not for the day. The error is an operator belt at the bakery. The street has already described you.

The bag at the door, to leave or to wait three days if the building says to come down. It looks like travel. Two to three liters of water. A way to treat more: a filter, tablets, or the boil plan, already rehearsed. Three days of food you eat with no fire and the mouth already accepts. A poncho, a blanket, dry socks, one set of clothes from the street you are on. A torch and cells that are not the phone’s. Document copies and contacts on paper. Cash. Gauze, gloves, and the house medicine. A power bank. A paper map. Minimal hygiene and a trash bag. A battery radio, if it fits. The family’s meeting point in one line, not in an app.
Ring three — the house, if you stay

Staying is plan A on most Brazilian Tuesdays. Water: three liters per person per day, fourteen days before you dream of ninety. More in the heat. Food the house already eats, with rotation, not an anonymous can. A way to cook without power, if it is safe and you know how to shut the gas. Torch, cells, power bank. Two weeks of medicine. Soap, hygiene, trash bags. Small cash. Knowing how to shut water, power, and gas. A documents folder. A battery radio. The animal’s food, if there is an animal. The plan on one sheet on the refrigerator: point, deadline, one contact outside the city. A pantry nobody rotates is not a kit. It is weight.

It is not a bunker in the window. It is not a photo of the pack. It is not a weapon as identity, nor a recipe for use. It is not food nobody in the house touches. It is not a map only on the phone: GPS walks without a network, the drawing of the street does not. It is not dozens of tools you have never opened. The phone is the fourth item. A paper compass and a lighter, if you are leaving the city, come before the app. The first-aid kit goes inside this one, not instead of it.

Once a month, open the bag. The car water in the heat gets changed. The cell gets tested. The medicine that expired leaves. Put the pack on and walk to the corner. If the shoulder hurts, you took something out. If you cannot find the document in the dark, the bag lied. Whoever lives with you has to know where it is and what is not argued at the hour of leaving. The rehearsal is this: one night without power, one route on foot, the bag in its place. No audience.
